Visit note | 2025-11-01 04:30 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Nabila Hasan, 52, female. Mrs. Hasan comes in for a review visit reporting that she has been losing weight despite eating well and feels like her heart is racing. She mentions that these symptoms began after a stressful family event in Bashundhara. She works as an accountant and has Essential hypertension. She denies tremors, heat intolerance, or eye pain. On examination: pulse 109 bpm, BP 146/90 mmHg, weight 53 kg. Thyroid is slightly enlarged without nodules. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice given: avoid excess tea and coffee, and rest when the heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-11-02 10:00 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Afsana Sultana, 30, female. Ms. Sultana attends for her first visit complaining of acne, irregular periods, and extra hair on her face. She noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Khilgaon. She works as a police constable and reports no major comorbidities. She denies hot flushes or severe pelvic pain. On examination: BMI 28.5, BP 135/79 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 84 kg. Abdomen is soft and non-tender. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-11-02 10:00 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Abul Sheikh, 43, male. Mr. Sheikh presents for his first visit with a fear of dying, sudden attacks of a racing heart, and breathlessness during attacks. He states that his first attack happened at a busy market in Rajshahi. He works as a shopkeeper and has Hypothyroidism, noting about 8 panic attacks in the last month. He denies chest pain radiating to the arm or loss of consciousness. On examination: BP 132/74 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 76 kg. Neurological examination is unremarkable and mood is anxious. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-02 11:00 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Shapla Haque, 43, female. Mrs. Haque returns for a follow-up visit regarding cramping belly pain, symptoms that are worse with stress, and persistent bloating. She explains that her flares happen on long commutes through traffic in Khilgaon. She works as a beautician and has no known comorbidity. Pain score is recorded at 3/10. She reports no rectal bleeding or unexpected weight loss. On examination: pain score 3/10, BP 122/70 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 79 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-11-02 11:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Shyamal Mondol, 22, male. Mr. Mondol attends for follow-up reporting pimples and blackheads on his face and marks left after pimples. He notes that the condition flared after using a heavy face cream bought in Chattogram. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-11-02 02:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Habib Bepari, 45, male. Mr. Bepari comes for his first visit with severe aching in his bones and muscles and pain behind his eyes. He mentions it started after a week of stagnant rainwater around the house in Narayanganj. He works as a beautician and has no comorbidities. Investigations reveal a platelet count of 92000 per microlitre. Other vitals: temperature 103.2°F, BP 110/73 mmHg, pulse 107 bpm, weight 62 kg. Chest is clear and abdomen is soft. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-11-02 03:00 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Mahmuda Siddique, 37, female. Mrs. Siddique comes in for a follow-up consultation reporting that she has been feeling slow, tired, and experiencing notable weight gain. She explains that these concerns were found during tests for tiredness after moving to Narayanganj. She is employed as a textile engineer and reports no other major chronic illnesses. Her recent laboratory results show a TSH level of 15.1 mIU/L. During the clinical interview, she denies any chest pain, palpitations, heat intolerance, or acute mood disturbances. On physical examination today, her blood pressure is 129/83 mmHg, pulse rate is 92 beats per minute, and her weight is 93 kg. Her skin appears slightly dry, and deep tendon reflexes show delayed relaxation phases. Neck examination reveals a non-tender, symmetrically enlarged thyroid gland without palpable nodules. Cardiovascular and respiratory examinations are unremarkable. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued to adjust her ongoing hormone replacement therapy. She was counselled extensively to maintain a regular sleep routine, engage in light physical activity, and consume a balanced diet rich in micronutrients. Follow-up is scheduled in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH test to monitor her thyroid status.
